title: Publishing a repository is a separate choice
when: Project creation, clone, existing-folder adoption or later publication
need: A prepared Git repository can stay local. Skipping GitHub makes the publish prompt default to No — keep it local; a verified connection keeps Yes — publish to GitHub selected. Connecting GitHub does not require publishing every project. Clone and adoption share an explicit publication destination choice: read-only preserves fetching and disables Yoke publication through the checkout publication_read_only project setting; Git remotes and native Git behavior stay unchanged; legacy disabled push URLs migrate once to this setting and only those legacy values are removed; source writes state confirmed versus unverified access; Fork and Duplicate use supported owned destinations. Read-only projects can prepare lanes and merge locally, including with an origin remote; Yoke pushes still refuse publication_destination_read_only. Merge preflight refusals print their reason and recovery. Repeated setup reopens the same destination choice for a read-only project and preserves a configured writable project.
gap: JOURNEYS 4–5 currently makes pushing to GitHub sound mandatory. That edge should be reviewed against the supported keep-local path.
review: Explicit CLI publication choices survive adoption and separate-project routing. Installed Duplicate and actual Fork publication are verified. Fork Review blocks Apply when cached installation facts are unready and names the same unmet condition as Apply: source repository coverage with Contents and Administration access, or a personal installation covering All repositories with write access. Permission absence is never inferred from missing repository coverage. Apply refreshes access before checking; its durable report records the actual destination separately from the original source, even if later work fails. Independent installed acceptance of this access disclosure remains owed.
